metadata.wofost_engine: Wofost72_WLP_FD (water-limited, free-draining) for every region. Regions water_regime.csv declares irrigated additionally carry a PCSE StateEvent that irrigates on soil moisture, so they keep a live water balance and a drought signal rather than running as potential production. See metadata.water_regime for what each region actually used.
metadata.crop_parameters: pcse.input.YAMLCropDataProvider reading github.com/ajwdewit/WOFOST_crop_parameters, baked into the image at a pinned commit rather than downloaded at run time. Uncalibrated for US conditions: absolute yields are illustrative, the anomaly is the signal.
metadata.yield_anomaly_definition: (projection - baseline) / baseline x 100, where the projection is this season's Wofost72_WLP_FD run and the baseline is the median of the same run repeated over each year of 1995-2024 on that year's real daily weather, with identical soil, planting date, variety and engine. Using the same uncalibrated parameters throughout cancels most of the calibration error. yield_percentile_rank gives the projection's place in that distribution, which is the more robust statistic where the distribution is skewed.
metadata.season_completion: observed (planting -> last observed day) + node 1 forecast + climatology normals to maturity. forecast_fraction reports the share that was not observed. Normals complete only the tail of a season whose soil profile is already charged by real weather; they are deliberately not used to drive a whole season.
metadata.stress_overlay: None. Stage-specific stress is reported as day counts only; no yield adjustment is applied, so every yield figure here is pure WOFOST. Base WOFOST does not model corn heat-sterility at silking -- see README.md.
metadata.determinism: Deterministic and offline: a pure function of the input document and the committed tables. No network calls, no randomness, no wall-clock dependence.

climatology.source: Open-Meteo archive (archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive, models=era5), ERA5 reanalysis. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0.
climatology.method: Per-region mean of each variable by calendar (month, day) over 1995-2024, in pcse.base.WeatherDataContainer units, using node 1's conversions (IRRAD MJ/m2/day x 1e6; RAIN mm x 0.1; VAP Magnus on the daily mean dew point; WIND 10 m -> 2 m by a 0.033 m log profile, requested in m/s). 29 February is absent and falls back to 28 February.
climatology.pcse_convention: pcse.base.WeatherDataContainer: TMIN/TMAX degC, IRRAD J/m2/day, VAP hPa, WIND m/s at 2 m, RAIN cm/day. NOT PCSE's CSV file convention.

baselines.source: Open-Meteo archive (archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive, models=era5), ERA5 reanalysis. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0.
baselines.method: One Wofost72_WLP_FD run per year of 1995-2024 on that year's real daily ERA5 weather, with the same soil, planting date, variety and engine the runner uses for its projection. Real years are used rather than a mean climatology because averaging destroys the structure of rainfall, which is what the water balance responds to. The baseline is the median of these yields; the percentile rank is the share of them below the projection.

ia.method: rainfed (water-limited, free-draining): no irrigation events are scheduled, so the agromanagement PCSE receives is identical to the one every region in this bundle used before brief 0002. The eight unsplit states and the two rainfed strata keep that behaviour exactly
ia.source: agromet-bundles/crop-weather/regions.csv (node 1 owns the region set): this row is either a rainfed stratum, or a state whose irrigated share of harvested corn acres is below node 1's 20 percent split threshold and which is therefore not split at all

ks_irrigated.method: soil-moisture-triggered irrigation inside the same Wofost72_WLP_FD engine the rainfed regions use: a PCSE StateEvent on SM with zero_condition 'falling', firing when the profile has dried to trigger_depletion_fraction of its plant-available water, i.e. at SM = SMW + (1 - trigger_depletion_fraction) x (SMFCF - SMW) from this region's soils.csv row. The water balance stays live, so a drought still shows a signal here; a potential-production run would erase it. irrigation_amount_cm is the GROSS application depth in CENTIMETRES -- the depth the system applies, which is what extension application-depth guidance states. PCSE reads it as the irrigate signal's 'amount' and adds amount x efficiency to the soil, so at 2.54 cm gross and 0.85 efficiency the profile receives 2.159 cm net per application. Modelled supply is unconstrained -- no aquifer decline, no allocation limit, no pumping-capacity ceiling in extreme heat -- so the drought protection simulated here is an upper bound, not a forecast of what a well can actually deliver. See README
ks_irrigated.source: management-allowed depletion of 50 percent of plant-available water, and centre-pivot application efficiency of 85 to 90 percent: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Extension NebGuide G1850, Irrigation Management for Corn; application depth 0.75 to 1.3 inches for medium- and fine-textured soils, same publication, with 1.0 inch = 2.54 cm taken as the mid-range increment; 0.85 as the centre-pivot efficiency assumed for general planning purposes: K-State Research and Extension L915, Using Evapotranspiration Reports for Center Pivot Irrigation Scheduling
